panels.visual: The goddess Thetis dipping baby Achilles in the River Styx, holding him by one heel, glowing water
panels.caption: When Achilles was a baby, his mother dipped him in the River Styx. He became impossible to wound.

panels.visual: The baby Achilles held up, the water dripping, the heel dry with a tiny circle showing the dry spot
panels.caption: She held him by the heel, so the heel stayed dry. Later writers added this part: Homer never told it.

panels.visual: Paris the Trojan prince aiming a bow; Apollo's light guiding the arrow in a golden trail towards Achilles' heel
panels.caption: Apollo guided Paris's arrow into that one heel. Achilles died.

panels.visual: A modern doctor's diagram of the Achilles tendon at the back of the ankle with a label, Glauka wearing a stethoscope-like gag, pointing
panels.caption: We still call a weak spot an Achilles heel. The Achilles tendon takes its name from it.
